page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with a printer's ornament (a woodcut vignette of a book and a shield within foliage) below the text. Running head and page number at the top. At the foot right, the gathering signature "D E". Faint show-through from the reverse side lies in the lower half and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Prima intentione sufficienter de actione dixisse vi-debimur; quorumque in quae fit actio, & quomodo, quo quidem loco actionem late sumpsimus sive ea patienti noceat, sive profit. Secunda intentione vanam illam actionis passionisque reciprocationem, qualem Aristoteles posuit, expugnavimus: falsumque esse virtutem illam quae vinceret, vincendo debilitari demonstravimus. Tertia in quo consisteret primarum qualitatum natura luculentum fecimus: In quibus omnibus non contemnenda nec inutilia ex abstrusissimis naturae recessibus in lucem produ-ximus, quaeque non parum profutura sint viam in naturae secreta molienti. Quae idcirco hoc loco tum propter rerum affinitatem, tum propter justam li-bri mensuram in unum contulimus;

page.notes: Printer's woodcut ornament (book with shield and foliage) below the text; not transcribed as text. Faint show-through from the other side in the lower half of the page, left out. Spaced capitals "D E" at the lower right are treated as the gathering signature. The paragraph runs on beyond the page, so it has no closing mark here. Long s is given as plain s in "abstrusissimis" and "justam"; the scan shows the form that is printed as f-like in the first word. No doubtful readings.
